connection.start-at-login-desc: Launch app when you log in

helper.status-desc: Eliminates password prompts when connecting VPN
helper.explanation: The helper runs as a system service and handles VPN operations without repeated admin prompts. Requires a one-time authorization to install.
helper.manual-cleanup-summary: Helper button stuck or failing? Show manual cleanup commands
helper.manual-cleanup-hint: Run these in Terminal, then reopen this window — Helper status will refresh and "Install Helper" becomes clickable again.

network.dns-override-help: Multiple servers separated by comma. Empty = use server-pushed DNS.

tunnel-health.description: Periodic ICMP ping to verify the tunnel is actually carrying traffic. Three failures fire recovery: pool member rotation or single-connection disconnect/reconnect.
tunnel-health.ping-target-help: Empty = use default 1.1.1.1. Useful if 1.1.1.1 is blocked or you prefer pinging an internal target.
tunnel-health.detection-time-help: Max detection time = interval × threshold. Default 5 s × 2 = max 10 s. Larger values lower battery / data cost; smaller values catch dead tunnels faster but may false-trigger on flaky networks.

sleep-wake.description: When macOS wakes from sleep, the upstream NAT mapping for the VPN has typically expired and the tunnel is silently dead — packets black-hole through stuck routes until manually disconnected. These options auto-recover.
sleep-wake.reconnect-on-wake-desc: Force-reconnect within ~1 s after wake instead of waiting for the tunnel-health probe (~60 s).
sleep-wake.prevent-display-sleep: Prevent display sleep while tunnel is up
sleep-wake.prevent-display-sleep-desc: Uses macOS caffeinate -di. Trades battery for zero sleep-related VPN drops. Default off.

on-demand.description: Automatically connect — or stay off — based on the network you're on. Network Rules are checked first, top to bottom; the first rule that matches the current network wins. Any network no rule matches falls back to the Connect-on-Demand default. The engine toggle and the default behaviour both live there.

failover.description: When a connection holds multiple protocols, failover walks them in this order. Move a protocol up to try it first.

diagnostics.crash-reports-desc: Help improve Privycs by sending anonymous crash reports. SSIDs, API keys, IPs and file paths are redacted on-device before upload to our self-hosted backend.

backup.description: Export all connections and settings as an encrypted file. Use the same passphrase to restore on another device.
backup.import-warning: Importing replaces your current connections and settings.
backup.error-passphrase-too-short: Passphrase must be at least 8 characters
backup.restored-message: Backup restored. Please reopen the app to apply changes.

engine.auto-help: Let the engine choose and recover the best protocol for the current network.
engine.auto-on-note: The engine decides the protocol automatically. The manual order is hidden while this is on.
engine.decisions-empty: No decisions yet — connect to see what the engine chooses and why.

decision.recover_wait: Recovering: waiting for the link to settle
decision.backoff: Connection failed — backing off before retry
decision.captive: Captive portal detected — sign in to continue

split-tunnel.heading: Split tunnel (bypass)
split-tunnel.description: Traffic to these IP ranges goes around the VPN. WireGuard + OpenVPN; IPSec members skipped (server-side traffic-selector negotiation).
split-tunnel.bypass-cidrs-empty: Empty = no custom CIDRs (private-networks toggle still applies)

dns-override.label: DNS Override
dns-override.help: Empty = use the global DNS Override from Settings. Overrides only apply while this pool is the active selection.

confirm.delete-pool: Delete pool "{name}"? This cannot be undone.

precedence.heading: How this screen decides
precedence.body: On every network change the rules below are checked top to bottom — the first rule that matches the current Wi-Fi or wired network wins. If no rule matches, the Default behaviour pinned at the bottom applies. Rules are only evaluated while the engine and Connect-on-Demand are both enabled.

engine.label: Rules engine enabled
engine.help: When off, every rule below is skipped and only the Default behaviour applies.
engine.disabled-notice: Disabled by default in v0.9.13.4 after stability reports. Toggle on to activate. Existing rules persist.

master.title: Auto-tunnel rules engine
master.subtitle-on: Rules below decide when the VPN connects automatically. Turn off to disable all auto-tunnel behaviour.
master.subtitle-off: Auto-tunnel is off. Connect and disconnect manually from the Connect screen, or turn this on to let rules below run.

empty.heading: No rules yet
empty.body: Every network falls through to the Default behaviour below. Add a rule to override it for a specific Wi-Fi SSID, BSSID, or network type — routing that network to a Pool, a Connection, or No VPN.

fallback.heading: Default behaviour — when no rule matches
fallback.cod-help: Default behaviour for any network no rule above matched
fallback.static-body: When no rule above matches the current network — or when the engine is off — the VPN does not auto-connect or disconnect. Use the Connect screen to control the tunnel manually.

eval.heading: Current evaluation
eval.network-wifi-unnamed: Connected to Wi-Fi (name not yet detected)
eval.decision-manual: Manual control only — engine takes no action
eval.decision-rule-active: A rule matches the current network — engine is acting
eval.decision-no-match: No rule matches — engine takes no action

cod.no-ssids-except-hint: Connect-on-Demand will trigger on every WiFi.
